changelog: **Breaking:** Trellis workflow data (tasks, specs, journals, scripts) now lives in an external local store (default `~/.trellis-wiki`) shared across projects as one local Git repository. migrationGuide:
## 0.6.x → 0.7.x: External local storage

0.7.0 moves Trellis workflow data out of the code repository into a user-managed local store (default `~/.trellis-wiki`, one local Git repository shared by all projects).

### What changes

- Workflow data (`.trellis` tasks / spec / workspace / scripts / config) now lives at `<storage>/<project>/`. The code repo keeps a root locator config `.treills.conf.json` and a browse-only `.trellis` link.
- Journal and archive commits land in the storage repository; code commits stay in the code repository.
- Legacy in-repo `.trellis` layouts must run the explicit storage migration before template updates apply.

### How to migrate

1. Commit or stash pending work in your code repository.
2. Run `trellis update --migrate-storage` (optionally `--storage <dir>`, `--project <name>`; add `--workspace <name>` only if the old workspace has multiple developer directories and no `.developer`).
3. The migration copies and verifies your data, then switches the locator config and browse link. The original `.trellis` is preserved at `.trellis.pre-migration.<timestamp>/` — validate your workflow, then delete it at your leisure.
4. The same command refreshes platform integrations with external paths, preserving modified files by default. Review any skipped/customized templates before relying on the new runtime.
5. Commit the resulting deletions in your code repository yourself (the migration never commits your code repo).

### Rollback

Delete `.treills.conf.json`, restore the `.trellis.pre-migration.*` directory back to `.trellis`, and re-run `trellis update --allow-downgrade` with the 0.6.x CLI. The external copy is additive; removing it never affects your code history.
aiInstructions:
When helping a user migrate from 0.6.x to 0.7.x:

1. Check `git status` first: uncommitted `.trellis` user data should be committed or stashed before migrating.
2. Run `trellis update --migrate-storage --dry-run` to preview; the real run is resumable — if interrupted, re-run the same command, it continues from the persisted checkout-scoped checkpoint and never deletes the source.
3. Multi-developer legacy workspaces (several dirs under `.trellis/workspace/` with no `.developer`) need `--workspace <name>`; other developers' journals are preserved under `workspace/history/<name>/`.
4. Migration refreshes hooks/commands in the same invocation. Review preserved template conflicts, validate execution without the browse link, and tell the user to commit code-repo changes themselves. Git commit failures block completion; do not override identity or bypass hooks.
5. Do NOT move or delete `.trellis.pre-migration.*` automatically — it is the user's recovery copy until they choose to remove it.
